outcome: Severity of hypertensive disorders in pregnancy (preeclampsia without severe features, preeclampsia with severe features, eclampsia)
Maternal outcomes (placental abruption, HELLP syndrome, mortality, emergency lower segment caesarean section)
cohort: The study included 230 pregnant women with singleton pregnancies after 20 weeks gestation, divided into case (hypertensive disorders) and control groups.
finding: Elevated serum LDH levels significantly correlated with increased severity of hypertensive disorders in pregnancy and a higher incidence of adverse maternal (HELLP syndrome, mortality, placental abruption) and foetal (intrauterine growth retardation, mortality) outcomes.
mod_finding: Emergency lower segment caesarean section was noted as an adverse maternal outcome across all case groups.
gest_age: Participants were singleton pregnancies after 20 weeks of pregnancy, with most severe cases of preeclampsia and eclampsia prevalent between 34 and 37 weeks.
